why: The answer uses the right plan for this task, copying element by element in a loop, but it never creates the copy array with new and its bound i <= data2.length goes one index too far, so the code throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException and is not a correct copy.

concepts.why: It copies one element per index into a separate array, but leaves out copy = new int[data2.length] and its loop bound runs past the end.
It treats length as the last valid index, but the last element is data2[data2.length-1], so data2[data2.length] is out of bounds.
The header is a valid counted loop, but the <= test makes one pass too many over the indices.
int is only used to declare the loop index, so the answer makes no claim about int itself.
